rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The halogens are the salt-formers: diatomic, seven-electron, electronegative to a fault. Down the group the atoms swell, electronegativity and oxidising power sink (**F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂**), and the elements thicken from pale-yellow gas to violet-black solid. Each halogen displaces the halide of every heavier sibling — Cl₂ water turns KBr orange and KI blue-black.…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The dry-litmus proof*** — chlorine gas passed over dry litmus changes nothing; the same gas over moist litmus bleaches it instantly: water, not chlorine, makes the bleaching acid HOCl.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Salt-Formers on the Left Edge of the Table Group VIIA: F, Cl, Br, I (and At). Seven outer electrons, one short of a shell — hence the name **halogen** (salt-former). This topic covers their general characteristics, preparation, reactions with water, alkali and ammonia, oxidising character, bleaching action, and the uses of Cl₂, Br₂ and I₂.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 General characteristics | Property | Trend down the group | |---|---| | Atomic radius | increases | | Ionisation energy | decreases | | Electronegativity | decreases (F 4.0 → I 2.5) | | Oxidising power | decreases: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂ | | Physical state | gas → gas → liquid → solid (F₂, Cl₂ gases; Br₂ liquid; I₂ solid) | | Colour | pale yellow → greenish-yellow → red-brown →…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2 oxidising power. Cold dil NaOH -> NaCl + NaOCl; hot conc -> NaCl + NaClO3. Dry Cl2 does NOT bleach. Acid strength: more O, stronger acid (HClO4 > HClO3 > HClO2 > HClO). I2 dissolves in KI -> KI3.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Verified NEB 2024 (2m): Arrange HClO, HClO2, HClO3 and HClO4 in order of increasing acid strength and explain.** — Order: **HClO < HClO₂ < HClO₃ < HClO₄**. **Explanation:** acid strength depends on how easily the O–H proton is lost, i.e. on the stability of the conjugate base ClOₙ⁻.…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): What happens when chlorine is passed through (a) cold dilute NaOH and (b) hot concentrated NaOH?** — **(a) Cold, dilute:** chlorine disproportionates mildly: **Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaOCl + H₂O** — chlorine at 0 splits to −1 (NaCl) and +1 (NaOCl, sodium hypochlorite — household bleach).…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For the oxoacid-strength question, explain via conjugate-base charge delocalisation over more oxygens — the oxidation-state count alone scores half.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Oxidising power falls down Group VIIA because the growing atom holds the incoming electron less tightly and stabilises X- less in water — so every lighter halogen displaces every heavier halide, and fluorine sits at the top with an anomalously weak F-F bond making it the strongest oxidiser of all.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Halogens F/Cl/Br/I: diatomic, 7 valence electrons, most electronegative family. Trends down the group: radius up, IE down, EN down (F 4.0 -> I 2.5), oxidising power down (F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2), colour deepens (pale yellow -> green-yellow -> red-brown -> violet-black), mp/bp rise, state gas-gas-liquid-solid.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Bleaching powder, water chlorination, PVC pipes and photographic film all trace back to the same family — the halogens are the chemical industry's workhorses.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Scientific Definitions | Term | Scientific meaning | Example | |---|---|---| | **Halogen** | Group VIIA element, salt-former | Cl₂, Br₂ | | **Disproportionation** | Same element simultaneously oxidised and reduced | Cl₂ in NaOH → NaCl + NaOCl | | **Bleaching by oxidation** | Colour destroyed by nascent oxygen permanently | Cl₂ water on litmus | | **Hypohalous acid** |…  ·  ## 4. Detailed Explanation ### 4.1 Why oxidising power falls down the group - Oxidising power = electron affinity + hydration energy of X⁻ − bond energy. Down the group the atom grows, the incoming electron is held less tightly, and X⁻ is stabilised less in water — so F₂ grabs electrons hardest, I₂ barely.…  ·  ## 5.
